chunks: And from him, from some of our companions, from Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Taymuli, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Ja'far, who said:

Al-Ma'mun asked Al-Rida (peace be upon him) about the saying of Allah, Exalted and Mighty: "Do not expel them from their homes, nor should they [themselves] leave [the homes] unless they commit a clear immorality."
He (peace be upon him) said: "He means by the clear immorality that she annoys her husband's family. If she does so, then if he wishes, he expels her before her waiting period expires, he does so."
And if the divorce is irrevocable (bain), in which he does not have the right of return, it is permissible for him to expel her in all circumstances. What indicates this is what he narrated:
ai.seo_question: What constitutes 'clear immorality' allowing a husband to expel his wife before the end of her waiting period according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from the era of the Abbasid Caliphate, Imam Al-Rida (peace be upon him) clarifies that 'clear immorality' (fahisha mubinnah) in Surah At-Talaq refers specifically to a wife causing distress to her husband's household, granting the husband the right to expel her before the iddah concludes. This ruling is contextualized within the broader Shia jurisprudence of divorce, distinguishing between revocable (raj'i) and irrevocable (ba'in) divorces, where the latter permits expulsion under all circumstances due to the finality of the bond.
